content:
A Republican congressman running for a Senate seat in Iowa has faced relentless mockery on social media after shifting his stance on the Iran war.

On Monday, Representative Ashley Hinson posted a lengthy thread on X calling for an end to the conflict, claiming Iowans "shouldn't have to pay for the Iran war at the pump or the checkout counter."

While being willing to change one's mind in light of new evidence can be seen as a sign of intelligence and open-mindedness, Hinson's situation may be nothing more than political calculation.

The war, which began in late February, has so far cost nearly $40 billion and contributed to rising gasoline prices.

According to NBC News reporter Sahil Kapur, Hinson trails her Democratic opponent Josh Turek by 8 points in a poll, and had previously voted against House resolutions to end the war at least six times, including one just last week.

Many were quick to point out the political contradiction.

Her Senate challenger joined in the criticism, saying: "It's easy to tweet, but when you had the chance to vote to end the war, you chose not to."

Podcast host Tim Miller noted that Hinson doesn't actually need to prove she wants to end the war, since Congress is adjourned until after the November election.

Others piled on as well.
